content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — § 7.7 (p0032)**

Section 7.7 makes *Customer* pay "as liquidated damages and not as a penalty" 15% of annual Fees for **each week** an invoice is unpaid, triggered by a mere ten-day delay. This is uncapped — roughly seven weeks of delay exceeds a full year's Fees — so it lands in walk-away territory (LDs exceeding remaining contract value, triggered by a minor breach) and fails the fallback (a single early-termination sum capped at three months' fees).

Checks performed:
- § 9 termination contains no early-termination or minimum-fee charge (§ 9.4: Customer owes only accrued Fees, with refund of prepaids), so there is no double-flag with T4C.
- No Vendor-to-Customer service credits were flagged (those benefit us).

Redline (validated, preferred position): replace the LD with ordinary interest on proper, undisputed invoices at the lesser of 1%/month or the legal maximum, plus an express statement that Customer bears no liquidated damages or penalty — preserving Vendor's late-payment protection while aligning with § 7.3's dispute mechanism.
